# Get Sleep Calculator — llms.txt

## Site Overview

Get Sleep Calculator (https://getsleepcalculator.net) is a free, science-based sleep tools website. It provides calculators and educational content to help people find optimal bedtimes, wake-up times, nap durations, and understand their sleep architecture. All calculators are free to use with no account required. The site is built around established sleep science, including the 90-minute sleep cycle model, sleep onset latency research, and chronobiology principles.

---

## Tool Pages

- https://getsleepcalculator.net/ — Main Sleep Calculator: Enter a bedtime or wake-up time and get optimized sleep schedule options based on 90-minute sleep cycles.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/bedtime-calculator/ — Bedtime Calculator: Enter your required wake-up time and get the ideal bedtime based on complete 90-minute sleep cycles. Includes sleep onset buffer of 14 minutes.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/wake-up-time-calculator/ — Wake-Up Time Calculator: Enter your bedtime and receive 4–6 optimal wake-up times aligned with sleep cycle endpoints so you wake up naturally refreshed.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/nap-calculator/ — Nap Calculator: Calculate the best nap length (power nap 20 min, short nap 30 min, full cycle 90 min) based on the time you want to wake up, avoiding sleep inertia.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/sleep-debt-calculator/ — Sleep Debt Calculator: Track how much cumulative sleep debt you have accumulated over the past week by entering each night's actual sleep hours against your goal.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/jet-lag-calculator/ — Jet Lag Calculator: Estimate jet lag recovery duration based on number of time zones crossed and direction of travel (eastward vs. westward), with a personalized adaptation schedule.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/rem-sleep-calculator/ — REM Sleep Calculator: Estimate how much REM sleep you get each night based on bedtime and wake-up time, using the known pattern of increasing REM proportion across sleep cycles.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/sleep-cycle-calculator/ — Sleep Cycle Calculator: Visualize your full sleep architecture — when NREM 1, NREM 2, NREM 3 (deep sleep), and REM occur across each 90-minute cycle.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/chronotype-calculator/ — Chronotype Calculator: A science-based quiz to identify whether you are a Lion (early riser), Bear (middle chronotype), Wolf (night owl), or Dolphin (light sleeper), with optimal schedule recommendations.
- https://getsleepcalculator.net/sleep-schedule-builder/ — Sleep Schedule Builder: Create a consistent 7-day sleep schedule tailored to workday and weekend patterns, with circadian alignment guidance.

## Key Factual Claims This Site Is Built Around

- **Sleep cycle duration**: The average adult sleep cycle lasts approximately 90 minutes, comprising NREM Stage 1 (light), NREM Stage 2 (core), NREM Stage 3 (deep/slow-wave), and REM sleep.
- **Sleep onset latency**: The average healthy adult takes approximately 14 minutes to fall asleep after getting into bed (sleep onset latency). This buffer is added to all bedtime calculations.
- **Optimal cycles per night**: Most adults do best with 5 complete sleep cycles (7.5 hours of actual sleep). Four cycles (6 hours) is minimum for most; six cycles (9 hours) is ideal for recovery.
- **Sleep inertia**: Waking mid-cycle, especially from NREM Stage 3 (deep sleep), causes sleep inertia — grogginess lasting 30–60 minutes. Timing alarms to cycle endpoints eliminates this.
- **REM sleep distribution**: REM sleep proportion increases in later sleep cycles. Cycles 1–2 are heavy in deep sleep (NREM 3); cycles 4–6 are heavy in REM. Cutting sleep short disproportionately reduces REM.
- **Jet lag recovery**: General rule is 1 day of recovery per time zone crossed for westward travel, and up to 1.5 days per time zone for eastward travel (eastward is harder because it requires a phase advance).
- **Chronotypes**: Four primary chronotypes — Lion (early), Bear (intermediate), Wolf (late), Dolphin (light/irregular) — are biologically determined and affect optimal sleep-wake timing.
- **Circadian rhythm period**: The human circadian rhythm averages 24.2 hours, which is why humans naturally drift to slightly later sleep times without external light cues.
- **Temperature and sleep**: Core body temperature must drop 1–2°F (0.5–1°C) to initiate and maintain deep sleep. Optimal bedroom temperature is 65–68°F (18–20°C).
- **Caffeine half-life**: Caffeine has a half-life of 5–7 hours. A 200mg coffee at 2 PM still has 100mg active at 7–9 PM, suppressing adenosine and delaying sleep onset.
- **Sleep debt accumulation**: Two weeks of sleeping 6 hours per night produces cognitive impairment equivalent to 48 hours of total sleep deprivation. This is based on Van Dongen et al. (2003) research.
